paper.title: Investigation of the low-energy stereodynamics in the Ne(3P2) + N2, CO reactions
affiliations: Institute for Chemical Sciences and Engineering, Ecole Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), 1015 Lausanne, Switzerland

research.topic: Low-energy stereodynamics of energy transfer reactions Ne(3P2) + X (X = N2, CO) producing Ne(1S) + X+ and [Ne–X]+ via Penning ionization (PI) and associative ionization (AI).
objectives: Measure collision energy dependence (0.2 K–700 K) of PI and AI product yields.
Investigate orientation dependence of Ne(3P2) using magnetic field control.
Compare branching ratios and stereodynamics between N2 and CO.
Account for predissociation of vibrationally excited [Ne–X]+ complexes.
methods: Merged supersonic beam technique with magnetic guide for Ne(3P2).
Orientation of Ne(3P2) via external magnetic field (10 mT).
Time-of-flight mass spectrometry for product ion detection.
Wigner D-matrix transformation from lab-frame mJ to molecular-frame Ω populations.
Model for predissociation probability and PD-corrected AI/PI ratio.
key_findings: For N2, bare N2+ yield dominates over [Ne–N2]+ at all energies; for CO, [Ne–CO]+ dominates below ~100 K.
Steric effect (orientation dependence) disappears below ~50 K for both molecules.
Predissociation probability increases with collision energy for both systems.
PD-corrected AI/PI ratio ~1 for N2, ~2 for CO at low energies.
Difference attributed to accessible first excited electronic state of CO+ (A2Π) which does not predissociate, while N2+ A2Πu is energetically inaccessible.

reactants.description: Metastable neon, paramagnetic, J=2, guided by magnetic multipole guide.

states.label: A2Π
states.energy: 20 733 cm−1 above X2Σ+ (133 755 cm−1 above neutral CO ground state)

states.label: A2Πu
states.energy: 9166 cm−1 above X2Σg+ (134 826 cm−1 above neutral N2 ground state)

quantum_numbers.molecular_frame: Hund's case (c), Ω = projection of J on inter-particle axis

theory.framework: Hund's angular momentum coupling case (c) for transformation from lab to molecular frame.

models.name: Wigner D-matrix transformation
models.description: pΩ(θkB) = Σ_{mJ} p_{mJ} w_q |d^J_{Ω,q}(θkB)|^2, with w_q = 2 for Ω=1,2 and 1 for Ω=0.

models.name: Ion yield model
models.description: Total ion yield proportional to sum over Ω of pΩ(θkB) σ_{AI,PI}.

models.name: Predissociation model
models.description: Observed X+ yield = w_pd(E) * I_{NeX+} + I_PI, where w_pd is fraction of NeX+ that predissociate. Predissociation probability P_pd = w_pd/(1+w_pd).

models.name: PD-corrected AI/PI ratio
models.description: I_AI / I_PI = (I_{NeX+} + w_pd I_{NeX+}) / (I_{X+} - w_pd I_{NeX+}).

assumptions: PI is independent of Ne* orientation (based on rare gas reactions).
Electronic predissociation of Ne–CO+(A, v=0) is slow on experimental timescale.
Binding energy of [Ne–CO]+ similar for CO+(X) and CO+(A).
Long Ne–X distances during reaction justify treating X as atom-like.
references: Perugia group models (refs 39–43): anisotropic interaction potentials and complex coupling functions.

excited_state_energies.N2+ A2Πu: 9166 cm−1 above X2Σg+ (134 826 cm−1 above neutral ground)
excited_state_energies.CO+ A2Π: 20 733 cm−1 above X2Σ+ (133 755 cm−1 above neutral ground)

observables.description: Ion yields for associative ionization complex and bare molecular ion
Ratio of associative ionization to Penning ionization cross sections after predissociation correction

energy_dependence.N2: Bare N2+ yield dominates over [Ne–N2]+ at all collision energies. Angle-integrated ratio I(NeN2+)/I(N2+) < 1 across entire range.
energy_dependence.CO: At high energies (>100 K), ratio similar to N2; at low energies (<100 K), [Ne–CO]+ yield exceeds CO+ yield (ratio > 1).

steric_effect.description: Orientation dependence (steric effect) observed above ~50 K; disappears below ~50 K for both N2 and CO.
steric_effect.quantification: Ratio r(180°)/r(90°) = 1 below 50 K (no orientation dependence), ~0.5 at higher energies.

predissociation.description: Predissociation probability P_pd increases with collision energy for both N2 and CO.
predissociation.trend: Similar upward trend for both molecules.

PD_corrected_reactivity.CO: AI/PI ratio ~2 at low energies, decreasing to ~1 at high energies.

results.interpretation: Difference due to accessible CO+(A2Π) state (only v=0 populated, no predissociation), while N2+(A2Πu) is energetically inaccessible. CO+(A) increases total complex formation cross section.

figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.description: (a) Time-of-flight mass spectrum at 352 K, θkB=90° for Ne*+CO. (b) Experimental ion yields vs θkB in molecular frame. (c) 2D plot of NeCO+/CO+ ratio vs angle and collision energy.

figures.label: Fig. 2
figures.description: Angle-dependent ion yields for Ne*+CO (a,b) and Ne*+N2 (c,d) at 600 mK (a,c) and 352 K (b,d). Red: bare ions, blue: complex ions. Solid lines: fits using Eq. (5).

figures.label: Fig. 3
figures.description: Angle-integrated ratio of Ne–X+ and X+ ion yields vs energy for CO (red) and N2 (blue).

figures.label: Fig. 4
figures.description: Steric effect (r(180°)/r(90°)) vs energy for N2 (blue) and CO (red). Value 1 indicates no orientation dependence.

figures.label: Fig. 5
figures.description: Predissociation probability P_pd vs energy for CO (red) and N2 (blue), obtained by fitting Eq. (6).

figures.label: Fig. 6
figures.description: PD-corrected ratio of angle-integrated AI and PI yields for N2 (blue) and CO (red).

figures.label: Fig. 7
figures.description: Energy level diagram for Ne(3P2)+CO reaction showing vibrational levels of CO+(X) and CO+(A) for bare ion and complex.

equations.label: Eq. (1)
equations.expression: A* + BC → A + BC+ + e− (Penning ionization)

equations.label: Eq. (3)
equations.expression: A* + BC → A + B + C+ + e− (Dissociative ionization)
equations.description: Dissociative ionization channel (closed in these reactions)

equations.label: Eq. (4)
equations.description: Transformation from lab-frame mJ populations to molecular-frame Ω populations using Wigner D-matrices.

equations.label: Eq. (5)
equations.description: Total ion yield proportional to sum over Ω of population-weighted cross sections.

equations.label: Eq. (6)
equations.expression: I_{X+}(θ_{kB}, E_{coll}) = w_{pd}(E_{coll}) I_{NeX+}(θ_{kB}, E_{coll}) + I_{PI}(E_{coll})
equations.description: Observed bare ion yield as linear combination of predissociated AI complexes and direct PI.

equations.label: Eq. (7)
equations.expression: I_{AI} / I_{PI} = (I_{NeX+} + w_{pd} I_{NeX+}) / (I_{X+} - w_{pd} I_{NeX+})
equations.description: PD-corrected ratio of AI to PI cross sections.

limitations: Assumption that PI is orientation-independent is based on rare gas reactions, not experimentally verified for N2/CO.
Experiment cannot distinguish between formation of CO+(X) and CO+(A) electronic states; Penning ionization electron spectroscopy needed.
Timescale for electronic predissociation of Ne–CO+(A) is unknown.
Simplified model assumes threshold dependence in cross sections for CO+(A) vs CO+(X) without theoretical justification.
Loss of steric effect at low energies attributed to dynamic reorientation but not fully explained.
Binding energy of Ne–N2+(v=4) not known accurately enough to determine accessibility.

references.context: Recent work on cold and ultracold chemistry under controlled conditions.
Phenomena observable at very low collision energies: orbital resonances, quantum tunneling, reactant reorientation.
Molecular beam techniques for low-energy collisions: co-expansion, crossed beams at low angles, Stark/Zeeman deceleration.
Merged beam technique for observing shape resonances, state-dependent reactivity, stereodynamics.
Previous stereodynamics studies in crossed molecular beams at collision energies >300 K.
First study of cold collisions with steric control: KRb + KRb in optical lattice.
Oriented HD collided with D2 in intra-beam collisions.
Magnetically oriented Ne(3P2) used to study Ne(3P2)+Ar and Ne(3P2)+N2 by merged beam method.
Energy transfer reactions studied in the lab.
Extensive theoretical and experimental studies of PI, AI, DI.
Perugia group: Penning ionization electron spectroscopy and theoretical modeling for Ne(3P2,0) + rare gases and molecules.
Polarization of paramagnetic species in magnetic guide; populations of mJ states determined spectroscopically.
Hund's case (c) coupling, Ω quantum number definition.
Branching ratio sensitivity to magnetic field direction in previous studies.
Ne(3P2)+ND3 reaction branching insensitive to magnetic field direction.
Associative ionization leads to van der Waals bound charged complex [Ne–X]+.
Predissociation of AI ions fast on experimental timescale.
Penning ionization largely insensitive to magnetic field direction in Ne*+Rg reactions.
Even–Lavie valve with dielectric-barrier discharge for metastable Ne(3PJ) production.
Rotational temperature of molecules estimated ~20 K based on previous experiments.
Energy transfer from metastable Ne* to molecules can lead to substantial vibrational excitation of resulting ion.
Binding energy of Ne(1S)–CO+ calculated to be 491 cm−1.
Vibrational frequencies of bare molecular ions: N2+ 2207 cm−1, CO+ 2214.24 cm−1.
N2 and CO are isoelectronic with similar properties.
Binding energy of Ne(1S)–N2+ estimated to be 300 cm−1.
